_note: THE STUDIO RESIDENCE SEAM TABLE (studio-apps.md §5) — the fifth run of the residence playbook. routeChain (Core/Apps/web/scope.js, MODULE-OWNED: the Apps module is the policy owner of what a mounted app may reach) folds one dotted chain + the granted set into a VERDICT: `door` (an /edit/api endpoint, method + exact path — document names ENCODED, never spliced, so the door's own containment stays the authority), `local` (the two page-local seams the host itself serves: selection, toast), `storage` (the app's namespaced convenience plane), `forbidden` (a real seam the app lacks the grant for — the refusal NAMES the grant, which is the whole developer experience of the sandbox), `unknown_action` (a known area, an unknown verb — or a missing required arg), or `unsupported` (anything outside the closed list: the arm that makes the residence a residence). Grants gate PER CALL in this funnel — host code the app's closed grammar can never alter — so bypassing an install dialog changes nothing. The `egress` section pins the granted-host gate (HTTPS only, suffix-matched so `acme.dev` admits `api.acme.dev` and refuses `acme.dev.attacker.test` — the server residence's rule verbatim; zero hosts = no outbound at all), which gates BOTH the JSE `fetch()` builtin (RunEnv.egress → fetchFunnel) and `<api>` head blocks (ApiBlockOpts.egress — the funnel law applied at the block tier, closing the bypass where `<api>` called the transport directly). Single-runner corpus: the plane has one runtime, the web Studio host (the spend-corpus standing). Runner: packages/cli/test/studio-apps-scope.test.ts.
